My starting routine
The same 4 steps for every question
READ
Which function acts first? In fg, it is g.
INNER
Work out the inner output first, as a number or an expression.
OUTER
Put that output into the outer function.
CHECK
Is every input and output allowed by the domains?
5
Watch out!
The order of the letters decides which function acts first.
QuestionWatch forExample
Q 1, Q 2fg and gf use the same functions in a different order.fg(2) = f(g(2)); gf(5) = g(f(5)).
Q 3f2 means apply f twice.f2(3) is not f(3) × f(3).
Q 9, 11, 12An equation can give an answer the domain does not allow.Reject answers that break “x > 0” or “x ≥ 0”.
Q 14 to 16A composite needs the inner output to be allowed in the outer function.f(x) = xx + 2 cannot take −2 as an input.
Q 19 to 21For the domain of gf, f’s outputs must lie in g’s domain.g needs inputs > 3, so you need f(x) > 3.

fg(2) = ________    gf(2) =
Before you open a hint, write your plan in one line:
Hint 1 · Echo
Say it in your own words: “fg(2) means f of g of 2. g goes first.”
Hint 2 · Slicer
Step 1: work out g(2). Step 2: put that number into f. Then do the same in the other order.
Hint 3 · Roots
Ask why the two answers might differ: squaring then tripling is not the same as tripling then squaring.
YOUR TURN
Compare your two answers. Are they equal?
Use the hints one at a time. Try on your own before you read the next one.
Before you start
Read Section 1.3 of the coursebook: composite functions, the three important points in the box, and Worked examples 3, 4 and 5.
Challenge ahead
Q 19 to 21 ask for the domain of gf. Only inputs whose f-output g can accept are allowed.
